bull.b: A $1.1B backlog with management's 60%–65% conversion estimate provides multi-quarter revenue visibility and reduces reliance on near-term new awards. This backlog underpins 2026 guidance and supports predictable production planning, helping stabilize revenue cadence and resource allocation.

bull.t: Rapid Revenue and Gross Profit Expansion
bull.b: Triple-year revenue growth and materially higher gross profit show the business is scaling and shifting mix toward higher-margin spacecraft and services. Durable scale benefits unit economics, enables better absorption of fixed costs, and supports sustainable margin improvement as mission volumes increase.

bull.t: Expanded Space Communications Network via M&A
bull.b: Owning ground-station infrastructure and deep-space comms capabilities strengthens vertical integration, reduces dependency on third parties, and creates cross-selling opportunities for lunar missions and data services. This strategic asset base enhances long-term competitive positioning in space infrastructure.

bear.b: Persistent negative equity and materially higher debt constrain financial flexibility, elevate refinancing and dilution risk, and limit the company's ability to self-finance capex or absorb delays. This structural capital weakness raises execution risk for multi-year infrastructure investments.

bear.t: Negative Operating and Free Cash Flow
bear.b: Sustained cash burn necessitates external financing to fund operations, CapEx for constellations, and integration costs. Reliance on outside capital can pressure timelines, increase dilution risk, and constrain long-term investments unless operating cash turns sustainably positive.

Low gross margins limit internal cash generation and make profitability highly sensitive to mix and execution. Combined with deep net losses and volatile results, this reduces resilience to contract timing slips and raises the burden on backlog conversion to achieve durable profitability.
